hardware_summary: Dual-fuel (gas/diesel) auxiliary generator set aboard the FSRU (vessel: Karunia Dewata), fitted with a SOGAV (Safety of Gas Admission Valve) fuel-gas supply system feeding the generator's cylinders -- a DFDE-type (dual-fuel diesel-electric) marine auxiliary power plant; count/rating not disclosed in the source.
fuel_basis: A 2025 Politeknik Ilmu Pelayaran Makassar (Indonesian maritime academy) engineering thesis, based on direct onboard observation, documents a SOGAV malfunction that caused a 'fuel gas trip' in the Dual Fuel Generator, disrupting 'the fuel gas supply to each cylinder' -- direct technical confirmation the generator runs on fuel gas (in dual-fuel gas/diesel mode) during normal shipboard operation, consistent with the DFDE (Dual-Fuel Diesel-Electric) LNG-carrier/FSRU auxiliary-power design referenced in the thesis's own bibliography.
captive_summary: The FSRU Karunia Dewata carries its own onboard Dual Fuel Generator (DFDE-type, gas/diesel) providing the vessel's electrical power; a 2025 maritime-academy thesis documents a fuel-gas-supply fault (SOGAV/gas admission valve) in this generator during a May 2022 incident at Benoa Port, confirming gas-fired operation. No MW nameplate is disclosed. This is separate from the terminal's send-out relationship to the Pesanggaran Diesel and Gas Power Plant (PLTDG), which is an external grid power station the terminal supplies (not captive).
confirmed_how: Politeknik Ilmu Pelayaran Makassar thesis (Walajri Tri Putra Hamka, 2025), 'Upaya Meningkatkan Performance Dual Fuel Generator Guna Kelancaran Operasi Pada Kapal FSRU Karunia Dewata' -- an engineering-cadet paper based on direct onboard observation of the vessel's Dual Fuel Generator, describing a SOGAV (Safety of Gas Admission Valve) malfunction that caused a 'fuel gas trip', disrupting 'the fuel gas supply to each cylinder', during a May 7, 2022 incident at Benoa Port, Bali. The thesis's cited literature includes 'DFDE berbahan bakar utama CNG' (DFDE with main fuel CNG) and 'The DF-Electrical LNG Carrier Concept', situating the generator as a standard marine dual-fuel diesel-electric unit.

captive_summary: No public design, AMDAL/UKL-UPL, or EPC-scope document was found describing this terminal's electricity supply. It is reported as a small-scale (targeted 30 BBTUD) land-based LNG import/regasification terminal at Teluk Lamong port, Surabaya (a large, grid-served industrial port area), being built by PGN LNG Indonesia (via PT Lamong Nusantara Gas) and PT Pelindo Energi Logistik, with China's Furui LNG contracted for the plant EPC work and targeting operation by end-2028. No source found states whether the terminal is grid-fed (PLN) or carries any on-site gas-fired generation -- absence of a documented negative means this is INSUFFICIENT, not NO.

hardware_summary: Generator sets are confirmed as part of the FLNG's long-lead procurement scope (alongside cold box and compressor) under the USD43.04 million Limited Notice to Proceed Agreement with Wison New Energies (8 Sept 2023) -- count, rating, and fuel type not disclosed in any source found.
fuel_basis: Not established in any source found. 'Generator sets' are named as a long-lead procurement item for the FLNG vessel, but no source states whether they are gas-fired/dual-fuel or diesel. The facility is an offshore/moored FLNG (no grid access at the Fakfak-Bintuni concession site) processing its own feed gas (330 MMSCFD from the Asap/Merah/Kido structures), which is the class of project where on-site gas-fired generation is standard industry practice -- but that is a design prior, not a documented fact for this specific vessel, and the fuel gate requires a stated fuel, so this is scored INSUFFICIENT rather than YES.
